messages:
Sara Lee: Heads-up — brought up reranker-v2-small int8 PTQ on 'prod-rerank' split. Quick perf check shows NDCG@10 drop on long-tail queries (len > 200 tokens).
Tom Nguyen: numbers?
Sara Lee: Ran eval vs fp16 baseline. Summary:
```
baseline fp16: NDCG@10 0.421, MRR 0.312
ptq int8:    NDCG@10 0.386, MRR 0.295
delta: NDCG -8.3%, MRR -5.5%
long queries subset (>=200 tok): NDCG 0.398 -> 0.352 (-11.6%)
```
Anya Patel: yikes. Did you change doc formatting/truncation? PTQ sometimes hurts longer context.
Sara Lee: No formatting change — same tokenizer, same doc concatenation. But I did enable kv-cache packing in the runtime for the PTQ variant.
Tom Nguyen: Could be quantization-induced softscore collapse for long contexts. Any logits distributions?
Sara Lee: Pasting sample logits delta (first 3 candidates):
```
baseline logits: [2.12, 1.75, 0.98]
ptq logits:      [1.80, 1.69, 0.90]
softmax diff:    [-0.03, +0.01, -0.02]
```
John R.: small absolute shifts but could reorder. How many reranks per query? top-k?
Sara Lee: We rerank top-100 candidates from bi-encoder. But evaluation metric computed on top-10.
Anya Patel: Dataset: are there dataset shift/sampling differences? Maybe long docs have more noise.
Sara Lee: Same eval set. I reran with candidate truncation disabled (keep full doc) and also with query-only trunc to 128. Results:
- keep full doc: NDCG@10 0.356
- query trunc 128: NDCG@10 0.360
Both worse than baseline.
EvalBot: automated-run: rerank-eval/1718254321: finished, seed=42, samples=10k, runtime=2h12m.
Tom Nguyen: Try QAT or per-channel quant? PTQ recipe maybe aggressive. What quant backend?
Sara Lee: PTQ with symmetric per-tensor, calibration using 2k calibration set from train. Backend: xquant v1.2 (per-tensor symmetric).
John R.: Try per-channel and MSE calibration; also compare int8 dynamic vs static.
Sara Lee: Will run per-channel + KL calibration; also will rerun with candidate normalization (L2) before scoring to see scale sensitivity.
Anya Patel: Also sanity-check tokenizer differences: leading/trailing spaces, HTML cleaning. Sometimes doc prep changes for long docs (we truncate by sentences).
Sara Lee: Good call — found a bug: long docs were being sentence-split then rejoined with extra spaces -> token boundary shift. Fixing, retest.
Tom Nguyen: Great. If still fails, run a small ablation: disable kv-cache packing and PTQ together/individually.
Sara Lee: Plan: 1) fix trimming bug, 2) per-channel+KL PTQ, 3) ablation matrix (kv-cache on/off, candidate L2 norm on/off). I'll post updated evals later today. Thanks.
John R.: thx. ping if you need GPU.
